examples.en: This price is downright robbery.
Overcharging like that, he's nothing but a highway robber.

examples.ko: 그 가게 주인은 손님한테 날강도처럼 굴었어요.
examples.en: The shop owner acted like a robber toward customers.

examples.ko: 수리비를 열 배나 받다니 날강도 아니에요?
examples.en: Charging ten times as much for repairs, isn't that robbery?
People call that company a bunch of robbers.
I feel like I was robbed blind.

explain: 진짜 강도보다는 터무니없이 비싼 값을 받거나 뻔뻔하게 빼앗는 사람이나 가게를 욕할 때 많이 써요. 거친 말이라 공식적인 자리나 윗사람 앞에서는 피해요.
explain_en: It is more often used to scold people or shops that charge outrageous prices or take things shamelessly than for actual robbers. It is a harsh word, so avoid it in formal settings or around elders.

examples.ko: 축구 경기 중에 선수들이 몸싸움을 했어요.
examples.en: The players scuffled during the soccer match.
A scuffle broke out on the subway.
Let's settle it with words before it gets physical.
In basketball the jostling under the basket is intense.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 몸싸움 끝에 경찰서에 갔어요.
examples.en: The two ended up at the police station after a scuffle.
The game ended without any scuffles.

explain: 몸싸움은 말다툼과 달리 몸이 부딪치는 싸움이에요. 크게 때리는 '주먹다짐'보다는 가볍고, 스포츠에서는 몸을 부딪치며 겨루는 것을 말할 때도 써요. '몸싸움을 벌이다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: 몸싸움 is a fight with bodily contact, unlike a verbal argument. It is milder than 주먹다짐 (a fistfight), and in sports it can also describe jostling for position. It is often used as 몸싸움을 벌이다.

en: to shout; to yell; to cry out

examples.en: The kids are clamoring for a snack.

examples.ko: 사람 살려 달라고 아우성치는 소리가 들렸어요.
examples.en: I heard people crying out for help.

examples.ko: 콘서트장에서 팬들이 가수 이름을 부르며 아우성쳤어요.
examples.en: At the concert, fans shouted the singer's name in an uproar.
Consumers are crying out now that prices have gone up.

examples.ko: 시장 사람들이 한꺼번에 아우성쳐서 정신이 없었어요.
examples.en: The people at the market all shouted at once, and it was hectic.

examples.ko: 배고프다고 아우성치는 동생에게 라면을 끓여 줬어요.
examples.en: I cooked ramyeon for my sibling who was yelling that he was hungry.

explain: 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 시끄럽게 소리치거나 요구할 때 써요. 한 사람이 소리치는 데는 '소리치다'가 더 자연스러워요. 불만이나 요구가 크게 터져 나오는 상황을 비유로 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Use it when many people shout or demand something loudly at once. For one person shouting, '소리치다' is more natural. It is also used figuratively when complaints or demands burst out loudly.

en: to argue; to bicker; to row

examples.en: A customer and an employee are arguing over the price.
Yesterday I argued with my older brother over a game.
Please don't argue loudly in the middle of the street.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 계속 언쟁하다가 결국 자리를 떠났어요.
examples.en: The two kept arguing and eventually left the place.

examples.ko: 회의에서 언쟁하고 싶지 않아서 말을 아꼈어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to argue in the meeting, so I held back what I said.

examples.ko: 이웃과 주차 문제로 언쟁한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once had an argument with a neighbor over a parking problem.

explain: '~와/과 언쟁하다'처럼 상대를 넣어서 말해요. 대화에서는 '말다툼하다', '다투다'가 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is used with the other person, as in '~와/과 언쟁하다'. In conversation, '말다툼하다' and '다투다' are heard more often.

examples.en: Kids are chattering noisily on the playground.

examples.ko: 교실 안이 와글와글해서 선생님 목소리가 안 들려요.
examples.en: The classroom is so noisy that I can't hear the teacher's voice.
The market is bustling every weekend.
This restaurant is too packed and noisy, so let's go somewhere else.

examples.ko: 콘서트장 밖에서 팬들이 와글와글 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Fans are gathered noisily outside the concert hall.
When vacation ended, the school became noisy and lively again.

explain: '와글와글 떠들다'처럼 부사로도 쓰고 '교실이 와글와글하다'처럼 서술어로도 써요. 사람이 많고 시끄러운 장면에 어울려요. '조용하다'가 반대말이에요.
explain_en: It works as an adverb ('와글와글 떠들다') and as a predicate ('교실이 와글와글하다'). It suits scenes with many people and lots of noise. Its opposite is '조용하다'.

examples.en: I ruined the presentation and got blamed by my teammates.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 무례한 말 때문에 크게 욕먹었어요.
examples.en: That singer was heavily criticized for rude remarks.
I spoke honestly, ready to be criticized.
Sometimes you get criticized even when you do well.

examples.ko: 괜히 나만 욕먹는 것 같아서 억울해요.
examples.en: It feels unfair, as if only I am getting blamed.

examples.ko: 실수했다고 너무 욕먹으면 기분이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: If you get blamed too much for a mistake, it feels bad.

explain: '야단맞다'는 주로 윗사람에게 혼나는 것이고, '욕먹다'는 사람들에게 나쁜 말이나 비난을 듣는 거예요. 인터넷이나 뉴스에서 많이 쓰고 '욕을 먹다'로 띄어 써도 같아요.
explain_en: 야단맞다 is mostly being told off by someone above you, while 욕먹다 is hearing bad words or criticism from people in general. It is common online and in the news, and '욕을 먹다' is the same thing.

en: sowing discord; setting people against each other

examples.ko: 그 사람의 이간질 때문에 사이가 멀어졌어요.
examples.en: We grew apart because of that person's meddling.
Don't be fooled by the sowing of discord; ask directly.

examples.ko: 회사에서 이간질을 하는 사람이 제일 싫어요.
examples.en: I hate people who turn coworkers against each other at work most.
The troublemaking got so bad that the team mood worsened.
I still don't know who stirred up the trouble.
Two friends had a big fight because of someone's scheming.

explain: 말 몇 마디로 두 사람 사이를 일부러 갈라놓는 나쁜 행동에 써요. '이간질(을) 하다', '이간질에 속다'처럼 쓰고, 좋은 뜻으로는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used for the bad act of deliberately driving two people apart with a few words. It appears as '이간질(을) 하다' or '이간질에 속다' and is not used positively.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 우리를 이간질해서 사이가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: That person set us against each other, and our relationship soured.
Stay away from people who turn friends against each other.
You must not drive a couple apart with lies.
I really want to find out who stirred up the trouble.
There is someone going around sowing discord behind our backs.
Don't be shaken by words meant to split you up.

explain: 남의 사이를 일부러 나쁘게 만드는 일이에요. '~을/를 이간질하다', '두 사람을 이간질하다'로 써요. 같은 뜻의 '이간하다'는 주로 글에서 보여요.
explain_en: It means deliberately making a relationship between others go bad, used as '~을/를 이간질하다' or '두 사람을 이간질하다'. The same-meaning '이간하다' appears mostly in writing.

en: to grate on someone's nerves; to make provoking remarks

examples.ko: 그 애는 내 실수를 보고 이죽거렸어요.
examples.en: He sneered when he saw my mistake.
Stop sneering from the side and help me.
His sneering way of talking is really annoying.
My friend made snide remarks, and it made me angry.
I want to avoid people who tease with sneers.

examples.ko: 왜 내 얘기만 나오면 자꾸 이죽거려요?
examples.en: Why do you keep making snide remarks whenever I come up?

explain: 비꼬듯이 얄밉게 말하거나 비웃는 모습에 써요. 비슷한 말인 '빈정거리다'도 있고, '이죽대다'도 같은 뜻이에요. 듣는 사람이 기분 나쁜 부정적인 상황에서 써요.
explain_en: It describes talking in a mocking, annoying way, or sneering at someone. '빈정거리다' is a similar word, and '이죽대다' means the same. It is used in negative situations where the listener feels bad.

en: to shrink; to cower; to wither

examples.en: The baby was startled and burst into a shrieking cry.
Everyone burst into fits of laughter at my friend's joke.
The puppy jumped in fright at the thunder.
The roaring laughter could be heard all the way down the hall.

examples.ko: 주사를 맞자 아이가 자지러져서 달래느라 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The child shrieked at the shot, and it was hard to calm him.
The movie was so funny that I nearly died laughing.

explain: 소리가 갑자기 높고 크게 터져 나오는 모습에 써요. 주로 '자지러지게 울다, 웃다'로 말하고, 깜짝 놀라 몸이 움츠러드는 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes a sound bursting out suddenly and loudly. It mostly appears as '자지러지게 울다/웃다' (to shriek or burst into laughter), and can also be used for flinching in fright.

en: to chat; to have a chat; to gab

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 친구와 잡담하다가 선생님께 혼났어요.
examples.en: I got scolded by the teacher for chatting with a friend in class.

examples.ko: 우리는 커피를 마시며 한 시간 동안 잡담했어요.
examples.en: We chatted over coffee for an hour.
I make small talk with my colleagues for a bit before meetings.

examples.ko: 일할 때 너무 많이 잡담하면 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you chat too much while working, you can't concentrate.
I just came to chat.
Making small talk with a neighbor in the elevator feels awkward.

explain: '이야기하다'보다 가볍고 중요하지 않은 얘기를 편하게 나눌 때 써요. '수다 떨다'는 즐겁고 길게 떠드는 느낌이고, 잡담은 별 내용 없는 일상 이야기라 수업이나 회의에서는 부정적으로 들릴 수 있어요. 명사로 '잡담을 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is lighter than '이야기하다', used for casually trading unimportant talk. '수다 떨다' feels like chatting happily at length, while 잡담하다 is content-free everyday talk that can sound negative in class or at meetings. You can also say it as a noun phrase, '잡담을 하다'.

en: to interfere; to intervene; to step in

examples.en: Don't butt into other people's business so much.

examples.ko: 엄마가 제 옷차림까지 참견해서 조금 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's a bit hard because my mom even interferes with what I wear.

examples.ko: 옆에서 자꾸 참견하면 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you keep butting in beside me, I can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 제가 참견할 일은 아니지만 걱정이 돼서요.
examples.en: It's not my place to interfere, but I'm worried.
My younger sibling likes to meddle in her older sister's affairs.

examples.ko: 누가 참견해도 저는 제 길을 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Even if someone interferes, I'll go my own way.

explain: '간섭하다'와 비슷하지만 '참견하다'는 일상 대화에서 많이 쓰고, 달갑지 않게 끼어드는 느낌이 있어요. '남의 일에 참견하다'처럼 '에'와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 사람에게는 '오지랖이 넓다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '간섭하다' (to interfere), but '참견하다' is more common in everyday talk and carries a feeling of unwelcome butting in. It is often used with the particle '에', as in '남의 일에 참견하다'. For a person like this, Koreans also say '오지랖이 넓다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 의사처럼 행세하며 사람들을 속였어요.
examples.en: That person posed as a doctor and deceived people.
He goes around acting as if he's rich.

examples.ko: 친구가 다 아는 척 행세해서 다들 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend acted like he knew everything, and everyone laughed.

examples.ko: 높은 사람처럼 행세하는 태도가 마음에 안 들어요.
examples.en: I don't like the attitude of acting like a big shot.
Scammers call people pretending to be police officers.

examples.ko: 아무리 잘난 척 행세해도 실력은 금방 드러나요.
examples.en: No matter how much you act superior, your real skill soon shows.

explain: 실제와 다르게 어떤 신분이나 지위인 것처럼 굴 때 써요. '~처럼/~로 행세하다' 형태가 많고, 대부분 좋지 않은 느낌이에요. 단순히 '~인 척하다'보다 사회적 지위나 신분을 내세우는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone acts as if they have a certain status or position that is not really theirs. It often appears as '~처럼/~로 행세하다' and usually has a negative feel. Compared with plain '~인 척하다', it leans more toward putting on a social status or identity.
